decision.parquet: no-go for adoption in this study: neither pyarrow nor fastparquet is installed in the existing Python toolchain; no dependency was added.
decision.threshold: Reconsider columnar storage only when repeated representative runs show at least 2x end-to-end benefit in the dominant workload or selective-column access is required at a volume where whole-record parsing is material, and the added dependency/runtime footprint is acceptable.

workload.comparedRecordShape: batch manifest run joined to riose-experiment-result v1 by runId

toolchain.note: Package installation footprint reflects only installed Python distributions; transitive dependencies and portability across target environments require a separate packaging study.

results.memoryMethod: process.memoryUsage heapUsed/RSS/external/ArrayBuffers sampled before and after each operation; RSS is process-level. Output includes last sample and is not a peak-memory claim.
results.selectiveReadMethod: JSON parses the full array before projecting fields. JSONL streams one line at a time and retains only the requested projection, but each selected row still requires parsing its complete JSON object; Parquet was unavailable.
limitations: One fixed scenario fixture is expanded into a deterministic 25-record (by default) batch; it is a representative experiment-runner record shape, not a survey of every future output contract.
JSONL and JSON contain identical full records; no fields, units, nulls, provenance or failures are dropped.
No Parquet results are reported because no Arrow/Parquet library is present in the current toolchain; no network install or new dependency was introduced.
Timing is specific to this host and includes local file IO; medians/spread are not cross-host product thresholds.
